doc_description: PepsiCo’s Q1 2023 earnings package reports 10% reported and 14% organic revenue growth, GAAP EPS of $1.40 (down due to the prior-year Juice Transaction) and Core EPS of $1.50, raises full‑year guidance to 8% organic revenue and 9% core constant-currency EPS growth, outlines FX headwinds and $7.7B in planned shareholder returns, includes detailed segment-level GAAP-to-non‑GAAP reconciliations, and provides investor call logistics with standard forward‑looking cautions.

structure.title: PepsiCo Reports First-Quarter 2023 Results; Raises Full-Year Guidance
structure.heading:
PepsiCo Reports First-Quarter 2023 Results; Raises Full-Year 
Guidance
structure.start_phrase:
PURCHASE, N.Y. - April 25, 2023 - PepsiCo, Inc. (NASDAQ: PEP) today reported results for 
the first quarter 2023.
structure.summary:
- PepsiCo reported Q1 2023 results on April 25, 2023 (Purchase, NY), citing resilient performance across categories and geographies.
- GAAP results: net revenue grew 10.2% with a 2.5-point foreign exchange headwind; EPS was $1.40, down 54%, with a 2-point FX impact.
- Non-GAAP (Organic/Core): organic revenue grew 14.3%; Core EPS was $1.50; Core constant-currency EPS rose 18%.
- Raised full-year 2023 guidance: organic revenue growth to 8% (from 6%); Core constant-currency EPS growth to 9% (from 8%).
- CEO highlighted strong momentum and continued investment under the “Winning with pep+” strategy—focusing on people, brands, supply chain, go-to-market, and digitization to build competitive advantages.
- Notes that guidance is provided on a non-GAAP basis due to unpredictability of FX and commodity mark-to-market impacts; refers readers to the Q1 2023 Form 10-Q and glossary for definitions and additional details.

structure.title: Summary First-Quarter 2023 Performance
structure.heading: Summary First -Quarter 2023 Performance
structure.start_phrase: (a)Excludes the impact of acquisitions and divestitures .
structure.summary:
- Scope: Summary of first-quarter 2023 performance by PepsiCo business segments and regions, covering revenue/volume, operating profit, and EPS, with GAAP and non-GAAP views.
- Revenue and volume:
  - Presents GAAP reported net revenue change and organic revenue growth, with percentage-point impacts from foreign exchange (FX) translation and acquisitions/divestitures.
  - At the total company level: GAAP net revenue up 10%; organic revenue up 14%; FX impact approximately -3 points; acquisitions/divestitures about +1 point.
  - Segment highlights indicate broad-based growth: strong double-digit growth at Frito-Lay North America; growth at Quaker Foods North America and PepsiCo Beverages North America; double-digit growth in Latin America; mixed results in Europe, Africa/Middle East/South Asia (AMESA), and Asia Pacific/Australia/New Zealand/China (APAC), with FX a notable headwind in certain regions.
- Operating profit and EPS:
  - Bridges GAAP reported % change to core constant currency (non-GAAP) by isolating items affecting comparability and FX translation.
  - Total company: GAAP operating profit down 50%, but core constant currency operating profit up 19%; GAAP EPS down 54%, but core constant currency EPS up 18%.
  - Key segment notes:
    - Frito-Lay North America: GAAP operating profit +23%; core constant currency +24%.
    - Quaker Foods North America: GAAP +18%; core constant currency +19%.
    - PepsiCo Beverages North America: GAAP -86%; after items and FX, core constant currency +10%.
    - Latin America: GAAP +13%; after adjustments, core constant currency +6%.
    - Europe: GAAP not meaningful (due to prior-year impairment/charges); core constant currency +159%.
    - AMESA: GAAP -6%; core constant currency +11%.
    - APAC: GAAP +5.5%; core constant currency +11%.
    - Corporate unallocated expenses: GAAP +132%; core constant currency +30%.
- Footnotes and methodology:
  - Volume excludes the impact of acquisitions/divestitures and may differ from organic volume due to product mix, nonconsolidated joint venture volume, and timing differences between bottler case sales (BCS) and concentrate shipments/equivalents (CSE); franchise-owned beverage net revenue is reported on a CSE basis; JV volume does not directly impact net revenue.
  - “n/m” denotes not meaningful due to 2022 impairment and other charges.
  - Results may not sum due to rounding.
  - Organic revenue and core constant currency are non-GAAP measures; reconciliations and definitions are referenced.

structure.title: Guidance and Outlook
structure.heading: Guidance and Outlook
structure.start_phrase:
The Company provides guidance on a non-GAAP basis as we cannot predict certain elements which are 
included in reported GAAP results, including the impact of foreign exchange translation and commodity 
mark-to-market net impacts.
structure.summary:
The document outlines PepsiCo’s updated 2023 guidance issued on a non-GAAP basis due to unpredictability of FX translation and commodity mark-to-market impacts. The company now expects 8% organic revenue growth (up from 6%) and 9% core constant currency EPS growth (up from 8%). It maintains expectations for a 20% core annual effective tax rate and approximately $7.7 billion in total cash returns to shareholders ($6.7 billion in dividends and $1.0 billion in share repurchases). A roughly 2-percentage-point FX translation headwind is anticipated for reported net revenue and core EPS. This guidance implies 2023 core EPS of $7.27 (previously $7.20), a 7% increase versus 2022 core EPS of $6.79.

The document also provides logistics for first-quarter 2023 investor communications: prepared management remarks (PDF) to be posted at 6:30 a.m. ET on April 25, 2023, and a live Q&A webcast at 8:15 a.m. ET the same day, with details at www.pepsico.com/investors. Investor and media contact emails are provided (investor@pepsico.com and pepsicomediarelations@pepsico.com).

structure.title: Prepared Management Remarks and Live Question and Answer Webcast
structure.heading: Prepared Management Remarks and Live Question and Answer Webcast
structure.start_phrase:
At approximately 6:30 a.m. (Eastern time) on April 25, 2023 , the Company will post prepared 
management remarks (in pdf format) of its first quarter 2023 results and business update, including its 
outlook for 2023 , at www.pepsico.com/investors .
structure.summary:
- The company provides guidance on a non-GAAP basis due to unpredictability of certain GAAP elements (FX translation and commodity mark-to-market).
- FY2023 outlook raised: organic revenue growth to 8% (from 6%) and core constant currency EPS growth to 9% (from 8%).
- Reaffirmed: core annual effective tax rate of 20% and total cash returns to shareholders of about $7.7 billion (dividends $6.7 billion; share repurchases $1.0 billion).
- Continues to expect roughly a 2-percentage-point FX translation headwind to reported net revenue and core EPS growth.
- Implies 2023 core EPS of $7.27 (up from $7.20), a 7% increase versus 2022 core EPS of $6.79.
- Investor communications: prepared remarks posted April 25, 2023 at 6:30 a.m. ET; live investor/analyst Q&A at 8:15 a.m. ET; details at pepsico.com/investors. Investor Relations and Media contacts provided via email.
- Q1 2023 results (12 weeks ended March 25, 2023 vs. March 19, 2022):
  - Net revenue: $17.846B vs. $16.200B (growth year over year).
  - Gross profit: $9.858B vs. $8.767B.
  - SG&A: $7.229B vs. $6.580B, primarily due to higher selling and distribution costs.
  - Operating profit: $2.629B vs. $5.267B; prior year benefited from a $3.322B gain from the Juice Transaction and included $242M impairment charges related to certain juice and dairy brands in Russia.
  - Net income attributable to the company: $1.932B vs. $4.261B; diluted EPS: $1.40 vs. $3.06.
  - Other pension/retiree medical income declined; net interest expense modestly improved.
- Notes on prior-year items:
  - Juice Transaction (2022): sale of Tropicana, Naked, and select juice brands to PAI Partners for $3.5B in cash plus a 39% noncontrolling interest in a North America/Europe JV.
  - 2022 impairment charges of $242M tied to brand repositioning/discontinuation in Russia.

structure.title: Condensed Consolidated Statement of Income
structure.heading: Condensed Consolidated Statement of Income
structure.start_phrase:
(a)The increase in selling, general and administrative expenses for the 12 weeks ended March 25, 2023 , as compared to the 12 weeks ended March 19, 2022 , 
primarily reflects higher selling and distribution costs.
structure.summary:
- Unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements for PepsiCo for the 12 weeks ended March 25, 2023 and March 19, 2022, including income statement, segment results, cash flows, and balance sheet, plus explanatory notes.
- Income statement highlights:
  - Net revenue increased to $17.846B from $16.200B; gross profit rose to $9.858B from $8.767B.
  - SG&A increased to $7.229B (driven primarily by higher selling and distribution costs).
  - Prior-year included a $3.322B gain from the Juice Transaction and $242M of intangible asset impairments (mainly related to certain juice and dairy brands in Russia).
  - Operating profit declined to $2.629B from $5.267B due to the lapping of the prior-year gain.
  - Net income attributable to PepsiCo was $1.932B vs. $4.261B; diluted EPS $1.40 vs. $3.06; weighted-average diluted shares 1,384M vs. 1,391M.
- Segment performance (12 weeks):
  - Net revenue: FLNA $5.583B; QFNA $0.777B; PBNA $5.798B; Latin America $1.777B; Europe $1.886B; AMESA $1.019B; APAC/ANZ/China $1.006B; Total $17.846B.
  - Operating profit/(loss): FLNA $1.599B; QFNA $188M; PBNA $483M (vs. $3.434B in prior year, reflecting the Juice Transaction impact); Latin America $364M; Europe $71M (improved from a $136M loss); AMESA $168M; APAC/ANZ/China $227M; Corporate unallocated expenses $(471)M. Total operating profit $2.629B vs. $5.267B.
- Cash flows (12 weeks):
  - Operating activities: net cash used $(392)M vs. $(174)M; key drivers include working capital outflows (notably accounts payable and other current liabilities down $2.259B), D&A $590M, pension contributions $175M.
  - Investing activities: net cash used $(532)M vs. provided $2.955B in prior year; 2022 benefited from $3.456B Juice Transaction proceeds; 2023 capex $581M.
  - Financing activities: net cash provided $777M vs. used $(1.780)B; 2023 included $2.986B of long-term debt issuance; dividends paid $1.608B; share repurchases $160M.
  - Cash and cash equivalents decreased by $263M in 2023 period to $4.837B; non-cash ROU lease assets obtained $213M.
- Balance sheet (3/25/2023 vs. 12/31/2022):
  - Total assets $93.0B (up from $92.2B); cash $4.770B; short-term investments $0.434B; receivables $10.469B; inventories $5.697B; goodwill $18.089B; other indefinite-lived intangibles $14.273B.
  - Total liabilities $75.867B (up from $74.914B); current liabilities $25.837B; long-term debt $37.486B (up from $35.657B).
  - Total equity $17.175B (slightly down); retained earnings $68.142B; accumulated other comprehensive loss $(15.601)B; treasury stock reflects 489 shares repurchased (in excess of par).

structure.title: Non-GAAP Measures
structure.heading: Non-GAAP Measures
structure.start_phrase:
In discussing financial results and guidance, the Company refers to the following measures which are not in accordance with 
U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP): organic revenue growth, core results and core constant currency 
results.
structure.summary:
- Explains the company’s use of non-GAAP financial measures—organic revenue growth, core results, and core constant currency results—for internal planning, performance evaluation, and compensation, and to provide investors added transparency and comparability of underlying trends.
- Emphasizes non-GAAP measures are supplemental, not a substitute for GAAP, and may not be comparable to those of other companies.
- Outlines the policy for adjustments, considering quantitative and qualitative factors, with typical items including: non-cash mark-to-market gains/losses; restructuring charges; acquisition and divestiture-related charges and gains; asset impairments (non-cash); pension and retiree medical settlements/curtailments; impacts from new laws/regulations (e.g., tax changes); tax position resolutions; tax benefits from reorganizations; debt redemptions/tenders/exchanges; and remeasurement of net monetary assets.
- Provides a glossary of key terms:
  - Acquisitions and divestitures: M&A, divestitures, and structural ownership/control changes in consolidated subsidiaries and nonconsolidated equity investees.
  - Bottler case sales (BCS): Physical beverage volume shipped to retailers and independent distributors by the company and independent bottlers.
  - Concentrate shipments and equivalents (CSE): Physical beverage volume shipped to independent bottlers.
  - Constant currency: Methodology to restate results at prior-year average FX rates using current-year results and FX rates.
  - Core: Non-GAAP results excluding specified items, with references to MD&A in the Q1 2023 Form 10-Q and 2022 Form 10-K for details.
- Details items excluded from core results for the periods presented:
  - Mark-to-market net impact on commodity derivatives recorded in corporate unallocated expenses, later reflected in divisions when underlying commodity costs are recognized.
  - Restructuring and impairment charges related to the multi-year productivity plan announced in 2019 and extended through 2028.
  - Acquisition and divestiture-related charges, including merger/integration costs and divestiture transaction expenses (consulting, advisory, and other professional fees).

nodes.title: Non-GAAP Measures - Introduction
nodes.heading: Non-GAAP Measures
nodes.start_phrase:
In discussing financial results and guidance, the Company refers to the following measures which are not in accordance with 
U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP): organic revenue growth, core results and core constant currency 
results.
nodes.summary: This section introduces the Company’s non-GAAP measures—organic revenue growth, core results, and core constant currency results—used for internal operating and strategic decisions, annual planning, business performance evaluation, and certain employee compensation. It explains that these measures aim to enhance transparency and comparability of historical and underlying trends, with adjustments determined using quantitative and qualitative factors. Potential adjustments include non-cash mark-to-market gains/losses, restructuring charges, acquisition/divestiture charges and gains, asset impairments, pension and retiree medical settlements/curtailments, impacts of new laws and tax changes, tax position resolutions, tax benefits from reorganizations, debt redemptions and tender/exchange offers, and remeasurements of net monetary assets. The Company cautions that non-GAAP information is supplemental, not a GAAP substitute, and may not be comparable to measures used by other companies.

nodes.title: Glossary
nodes.heading: Glossary
nodes.start_phrase:
We use the following definitions when referring to our non-GAAP financial measures, which may not be the same as or 
comparable to similar measures presented by other companies:
nodes.summary:
- Overview of the company’s use of non-GAAP financial measures—organic revenue growth, core results, and core constant currency results—including why management uses them (operational decision-making, performance evaluation, compensation) and why they are provided to investors (comparability, transparency).
- Caution that non-GAAP measures are supplemental, not a substitute for GAAP, and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies.
- Framework for considering adjustments: qualitative and quantitative factors used to decide when to adjust for significant or trend-distorting items.
- Glossary of non-GAAP terms and metrics:
  - Acquisitions and divestitures (including structural changes).
  - Bottler case sales (BCS) and concentrate shipments and equivalents (CSE).
  - Constant currency methodology.
  - Core results definition and referenced sources for excluded items.
  - Effective net pricing.
  - Organic revenue growth and rationale for its use.
- Detailed list of items excluded from “core” results:
  - Mark-to-market net gains/losses on commodity derivatives (recorded in corporate, later reflected in divisions).
  - Restructuring and impairment charges tied to the multi-year productivity plan (extended through 2028).
  - Acquisition and divestiture-related charges (merger/integration and transaction costs).
  - Gain on the Juice Transaction (recognized in PBNA and Europe).
  - Impairment and other charges/credits:
    - Russia-Ukraine conflict charges (asset impairments, credit losses, inventory write-downs, other costs).
    - Brand portfolio impairments and related actions (including sale/discontinuation decisions and prior-year adjustments).
    - Other impairment charges (indefinite-lived intangibles driven by higher WACC and updated outlooks).
  - Pension and retiree medical-related impacts (settlements/curtailments).
  - Tax items: IRS audit-related tax benefit (2014–2019) and TCJ Act transition tax adjustments.
- 2023 guidance framework:
  - Organic revenue growth excludes FX, M&A/divestitures, and the 2022 53rd week.
  - Core effective tax rate and core constant currency EPS growth exclude mark-to-market, restructuring/impairment, and specified items; core constant currency EPS also excludes FX.
  - Company cannot reconcile projected non-GAAP guidance to GAAP due to unpredictability of FX, commodity prices, and M&A/divestitures.
- Reconciliation schedule provided for Q1 2023 (12 weeks ended March 25, 2023) showing reported vs. organic revenue growth by segment and drivers (organic volume and effective net pricing), with key highlights:
  - Frito-Lay North America: 15% reported; 16% organic; pricing-driven.
  - Quaker Foods North America: 9% reported; 10% organic; volume down, pricing up.
  - PepsiCo Beverages North America: 8% reported; 12% organic; includes acquisition/divestiture impacts.
  - Latin America: 21% reported; 16% organic; strong pricing.
  - Europe: 5% reported; 14% organic; significant pricing offset by volume decline; M&A impact noted.
  - Africa, Middle East and South Asia: 2% reported; 29% organic; strong pricing.
  - APAC/ANZ/China: (1%) reported; 4% organic; modest gains.
  - Total company: 10% reported; 14% organic; approximate FX impact 2.5% and M&A impact 2%, with pricing the primary driver.
- Notes clarifying that acquisitions/divestitures primarily reflect the Juice Transaction; organic volume excludes M&A; differences between volume metrics may arise from mix, JV volume, and BCS vs. CSE timing; amounts may not sum due to rounding.

structure.title: Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Information
structure.heading: Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Information
structure.start_phrase: (a)Acquisitions and divestitures primarily reflect the Juice Transaction in PepsiCo Beverages North America and Europe.
structure.summary:
- PepsiCo’s unaudited reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP (organic) revenue growth for the 12 weeks ended March 25, 2023.
- Presents, by operating segment and in total: reported net revenue year-over-year % change (GAAP), impacts of foreign exchange and acquisitions/divestitures, resulting organic revenue % change (Non-GAAP), and the split of organic growth between volume and effective net pricing.
- Company-wide highlights:
  - Total reported revenue growth: +10%; after FX and M&A adjustments, organic revenue growth: +14%.
  - Organic growth driven primarily by pricing (+16 pts) with a modest volume decline (-2 pts).
- Segment highlights (organic, Non-GAAP):
  - Frito-Lay North America: +16% organic; growth entirely from pricing (volume flat).
  - Quaker Foods North America: +10% organic; pricing +15 pts, volume -5 pts.
  - PepsiCo Beverages North America: +12% organic; pricing +15 pts, volume -3 pts; acquisitions/divestitures impact reflects the Juice Transaction.
  - Latin America: +16% organic; pricing +15 pts, volume +1 pt; FX impact noted.
  - Europe: +14% organic; pricing +23 pts, volume -9 pts; FX and Juice Transaction impacts noted.
  - Africa, Middle East and South Asia: +29% organic; pricing +31 pts, volume -2 pts; significant FX impact noted.
  - Asia Pacific, Australia/New Zealand and China Region: +4% organic; pricing +2.5 pts, volume +2 pts; FX impact noted.
- Footnotes and clarifications:
  - Acquisitions/divestitures impacts primarily reflect the Juice Transaction in PBNA and Europe.
  - “Organic volume” excludes M&A and may differ from other reported volume metrics due to product mix, nonconsolidated JV volume, and timing differences in franchise-owned beverage businesses (BCS vs. CSE); JV volume does not directly impact net revenue.
  - Non-GAAP measure discussion referenced on pages A-6 to A-7; figures may not sum due to rounding.

nodes.title: Organic Revenue Growth Rates
nodes.heading: Organic Revenue Growth Rates
nodes.start_phrase: (a)Acquisitions and divestitures primarily reflect the Juice Transaction in PepsiCo Beverages North America and Europe.
nodes.summary:
- Document scope: PepsiCo’s reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP metrics for the 12 weeks ended March 25, 2023 (unaudited), focusing on organic revenue growth and year-over-year growth after items affecting comparability and foreign exchange.
- Organic revenue growth by segment: Shows GAAP net revenue YoY change, adjustments for foreign exchange and acquisitions/divestitures (notably the Juice Transaction in PBNA and Europe), to derive Non-GAAP organic growth, plus its drivers (organic volume and effective net pricing).
  - Frito-Lay North America: 16% organic growth, driven by pricing with flat volume.
  - Quaker Foods North America: 10% organic; volume -5%, pricing +15%.
  - PepsiCo Beverages North America: 12% organic; volume -3%, pricing +15%.
  - Latin America: 16% organic; volume +1%, pricing +15%; FX -6%, M&A +1%.
  - Europe: 14% organic; volume -9%, pricing +23%; FX +5%, M&A +4%.
  - Africa, Middle East and South Asia: 29% organic; volume -2%, pricing +31%; FX +28%.
  - Asia Pac, Australia/NZ and China: 4% organic; volume +2%, pricing +2.5%; FX +6%.
  - Total PepsiCo: 14% organic; volume -2%, pricing +16%; FX +2.5%, M&A +2%.
- Year-over-year growth reconciliation: Converts GAAP reported changes to Core (Non-GAAP) and Core Constant Currency by adjusting for mark-to-market impacts, restructuring/impairment, acquisition/divestiture-related charges, gain from the Juice Transaction, and other charges/credits, then isolating FX.
  - Frito-Lay North America: GAAP +23%; Core +24%; Core CC +24%.
  - Quaker Foods North America: GAAP +18%; Core +18%; Core CC +19%.
  - PepsiCo Beverages North America: GAAP -86% (distorted by Juice Transaction gain); Core +9%; Core CC +10%.
  - Latin America: GAAP +13%; Core +12%; Core CC +6%.
  - Europe: GAAP n/m (due to prior-year impairments); Core +148%; Core CC +159%.
  - Africa, Middle East and South Asia: GAAP -6%; Core -12%; Core CC +11%.
  - Asia Pac, Australia/NZ and China: GAAP/Core +5.5%; Core CC +11%.
  - Corporate unallocated expenses: GAAP +132%; Core +30%.
  - Total operating profit: GAAP -50%; Core +17%; Core CC +19%.
  - Net income attributable to PepsiCo: GAAP -55%; Core +15%; Core CC +18%.
  - Diluted EPS: GAAP -54%; Core +16%; Core CC +18%.
- Definitions/notes:
  - Non-GAAP measures (Organic revenue, Core results, Core Constant Currency) referenced to detailed discussion on pages A-6 to A-7.
  - Organic volume excludes M&A; differences from other volume disclosures can arise from product mix, nonconsolidated JV volume, and timing between BCS and CSE in franchise beverage businesses; JV volume does not directly affect net revenue.
  - “n/m” denotes not meaningful due to prior-year impairments; amounts may not sum due to rounding.

nodes.title: Year over Year Growth Rates
nodes.heading: Year over Year Growth Rates
nodes.start_phrase: (a) A financial measure that is not in accordance with GAAP.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose: Reconciliation of PepsiCo’s GAAP and Non-GAAP (Core) results, including year-over-year growth rates and detailed line-item bridges for the 12 weeks ended March 25, 2023 (with prior-year comparison to March 19, 2022).
- Year-over-year growth by segment and at the total-company level:
  - Presents reported GAAP % change, adjustments for items affecting comparability (mark-to-market, restructuring/impairment, acquisition/divestiture-related charges, gain from the Juice Transaction, impairment and other charges/credits), resulting Core (Non-GAAP) % change, foreign exchange translation impact, and Core constant currency % change.
  - Segments covered: Frito-Lay North America, Quaker Foods North America, PepsiCo Beverages North America, Latin America, Europe, Africa/Middle East/South Asia, Asia Pacific/Australia/New Zealand/China Region, Corporate unallocated, Total Operating Profit, Net Income Attributable to PepsiCo, and Diluted EPS.
  - Key Core constant currency growth indications: FLNA +24%, QFNA +19%, PBNA +10%, Latin America +6%, Europe +159% (n/m on reported due to prior-year impairment effects), AMESA +11%, APAC/ANZ/China +11%; Total Operating Profit +19%, Net Income +18%, Diluted EPS +18%.
  - Notes that reported GAAP results show large declines versus prior year due to sizable 2022 items (e.g., Juice Transaction gain, impairments), while Core Non-GAAP shows underlying growth.
- Detailed line-item reconciliations for 12 weeks ended March 25, 2023 vs. March 19, 2022:
  - Provides GAAP and Core Non-GAAP amounts for cost of sales, gross profit, SG&A, operating profit, other pension and retiree medical benefits income, provision for income taxes, net income attributable to noncontrolling interests, net income attributable to PepsiCo, diluted EPS, and effective tax rate.
  - 2023 GAAP to Core adjustments include mark-to-market, restructuring/impairment, acquisition/divestiture-related charges, and impairment/other charges/credits.
  - 2022 GAAP to Core adjustments include mark-to-market, restructuring/impairment, acquisition/divestiture-related charges, the gain from the Juice Transaction, impairment of intangible assets, and pension/retiree medical-related impacts.
  - Illustrative Core results: 2023 Core operating profit $2,802m, net income $2,071m, diluted EPS $1.50, effective tax rate 21.7%; 2022 Core operating profit $2,392m, net income $1,795m, diluted EPS $1.29, effective tax rate 20.6%.
- Explanatory notes:
  - Non-GAAP measures defined and referenced to further discussion on pages A-6 to A-7.
  - Foreign exchange translation and constant currency methodology applied to Core results.
  - Tax footnotes explain expected tax on underlying items and the effect of comparability items on effective tax rate.
  - Notations for “n/m” (not meaningful) due to prior-year impairment impacts and rounding.

nodes.title: Certain Line Items
nodes.heading: Certain Line Items
nodes.start_phrase: (a)A financial measure that is not in accordance with GAAP.
nodes.summary:
- Document type: PepsiCo, Inc. and Subsidiaries – Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP information for select line items and divisional operating profit; unaudited, amounts in millions (except per-share data); 12 weeks ended March 25, 2023 and March 19, 2022.
- Purpose: Bridge from reported GAAP results to “Core” Non-GAAP measures by isolating items affecting comparability, and show their impact on key financial statement lines, diluted EPS, and effective tax rate.
- Line-item reconciliation (consolidated):
  - 2023 (12 weeks ended 3/25/2023): Adjustments include mark-to-market impacts, restructuring and impairment charges, acquisition/divestiture-related charges, and impairment/other credits. GAAP diluted EPS $1.40; Core Non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.50. GAAP effective tax rate 21.9%; Core 21.7%.
  - 2022 (12 weeks ended 3/19/2022): Adjustments include mark-to-market, restructuring and impairment, acquisition/divestiture-related charges, a significant gain associated with the Juice Transaction, impairment and other charges/credits, and pension/retiree medical-related impacts. GAAP diluted EPS $3.06; Core Non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.29. GAAP effective tax rate 17.2%; Core 20.6%.
- Items affecting comparability (described and quantified across periods and lines): 
  - Mark-to-market net impact.
  - Restructuring and impairment charges.
  - Acquisition and divestiture-related charges.
  - Gain associated with the Juice Transaction (notably large in 2022).
  - Impairment and other charges/credits.
  - Pension and retiree medical-related impact (2022).
- Operating profit by division (reconciled to Core Non-GAAP):
  - Divisions: Frito-Lay North America, Quaker Foods North America, PepsiCo Beverages North America, Latin America, Europe, Africa/Middle East/South Asia, Asia Pacific/Australia/New Zealand/China, and Corporate unallocated.
  - 2023: GAAP operating profit $2,629; Core Non-GAAP $2,802 after adjustments (notably restructuring/impairment and corporate mark-to-market).
  - 2022: GAAP operating profit $5,267; Core Non-GAAP $2,392 after removing the Juice Transaction gain and other adjustments (including impairment credits in Europe and corporate mark-to-market).
- Footnotes and methodology:
  - (a) Core is a Non-GAAP measure; referenced pages A-6 to A-7 for definitions.
  - (b) Tax provision adjustments reflect expected tax on each underlying item based on applicable jurisdictional tax laws/rates.
  - (c) Effective tax rate impact reflects differing tax rates on items affecting comparability.
  - Note: Amounts may not sum due to rounding.

nodes.title: Operating Profit by Division
nodes.heading: Operating Profit by Division

nodes.summary:
- The document is PepsiCo’s unaudited reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP (Core) financial measures, focused on divisional operating profit, margin metrics, and EPS.
- Operating profit by division for the 12 weeks ended March 25, 2023 and March 19, 2022 is presented, showing GAAP results and adjustments for:
  - Mark-to-market net impact
  - Restructuring and impairment charges
  - Acquisition and divestiture-related charges

structure.summary: The excerpt is a standard forward-looking statements caution from PepsiCo. It explains that statements about 2023 guidance and outlook are based on current information and plans, and identifies common forward‑looking terminology. It warns that numerous risks and uncertainties could cause actual results to differ materially, citing examples such as geopolitical conflict (Ukraine), demand and brand reputation, product quality and recalls, competition, talent and workforce issues, water scarcity, retail landscape shifts and key customer exposure, manufacturing and supply chain disruptions and cost inflation, political/social conditions, emerging markets growth, macroeconomic changes, cyber incidents, strategic transactions, reliance on third-party providers and enterprise systems, climate change and related measures, labor actions, failure to realize productivity gains, impairments, foreign exchange volatility, credit rating changes, new or increased product taxes and marketing limits, packaging and plastics regulations, data privacy compliance, income tax changes or disputes, intellectual property issues, compliance failures, and litigation or regulatory matters. It directs readers to SEC filings (Form 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K) for more detail, cautions investors not to place undue reliance on these statements, and disclaims any obligation to update them.
